raw.details:
Guidelines:

  • Eligibility: Open to students interested in software development, programming, web/app development, AI/ML, cybersecurity, data science, UI/UX, and related technical fields.
  • Team Size: Each team must consist of 2–4 members.
  • Inter-College Teams: Inter-college teams are allowed, subject to successful registration and approval by the organizers.
  • Inter-Specialization Teams: Inter-specialization/branch teams are allowed and encouraged. Students from Computer Science, Information Science, AI/ML, Electronics, and other relevant disciplines may form a team.
  • Event Type: 8-hour on-site software hackathon.
  • Number of Problem Statements: Teams will work on one problem statement, which will be revealed only on the day of the event.
  • Problem Statement: The challenge will involve developing a working software solution for a real-world problem.
  • Duration: 8 hours of development time.
  • Development Format: Teams must build their solution from scratch during the event. Participants should not arrive with a pre-built solution for the announced problem.
  • Submission: Teams must submit a working software solution within the allotted time.
  • Judging: Solutions will be evaluated through a live demonstration/judging session at the end of the hackathon. Recorded demos or slide-only submissions are not accepted.
  • Buffs & Debuffs: Four times during the event, a common wheel/spin will introduce either a helpful Buff or a challenging Debuff. The selected condition will apply to all teams for 30 minutes.
  • Fairness: The same Buff or Debuff is applied to all participating teams simultaneously and does not directly affect the scoring.
  • Technology: Teams may use appropriate programming languages, frameworks, development tools, APIs, and other permitted resources to build their solution.
  • Registration: Registration requires organizer approval. The registration fee is ₹200 per team, paid online by the team lead.
  • Venue: Ramaiah Technology Campus, Bengaluru.
  • Event Dates: 14–16 October 2026; the specific CHAOS slot is as announced in the official schedule.
  • Prizes: 1st – ₹15,000; 2nd – ₹10,000; 3rd – ₹7,000.

Rules:

  • Each team must consist of 2–4 registered members.
  • Teams must work only on the problem statement announced by the organizers on the day of the hackathon.
  • The problem statement will be revealed at the start of the challenge; teams must develop their solution during the allotted hackathon period.
  • Teams must build a working software solution rather than submitting only an idea or presentation.
  • Previously developed solutions that directly solve the announced problem must not be submitted as the team's original work.
  • Teams may use publicly available documentation, libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development resources unless specifically restricted by the organizers.
  • All third-party libraries, APIs, datasets, or other external resources used in the project should comply with their respective licenses and usage conditions.
  • Each team is responsible for ensuring that its submitted work is original and does not infringe the intellectual property of others.
  • Teams must submit their working solution before the official submission deadline.
  • Late submissions may be penalized or rejected at the discretion of the organizers.
  • Every team must be prepared to demonstrate its working solution live to the judges.
  • Recorded demonstrations or slide-only submissions will not be accepted as a substitute for a working solution.
  • Teams must not receive unauthorized assistance from other teams or individuals during the competition.
  • Sharing code or substantially assisting another team may result in penalties or disqualification.
  • Teams must not intentionally disrupt another team's systems, workspace, network access, development environment, or progress.
  • Participants must follow all instructions issued by the organizers and event coordinators.
  • The Buffs & Debuffs wheel will be conducted four times during the event. The resulting condition will apply equally to all teams for the specified 30-minute period.
  • Participants must follow the announced Buff or Debuff condition during the applicable period.
  • Teams must not exploit a Buff or Debuff in a way that compromises another team's work, venue infrastructure, or event systems.
  • Any form of cheating, plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, malicious activity, or deliberate rule violation may result in immediate disqualification.
  • Participants must not use their software skills to attack, damage, or gain unauthorized access to systems, networks, accounts, or data.
  • Teams are responsible for maintaining backups of their project and source code.
  • Participants must maintain proper conduct toward judges, organizers, volunteers, sponsors, and other teams.
  • Any damage to venue property, equipment, or infrastructure caused intentionally or through serious negligence may result in penalties.
  • Judges may evaluate submissions based on factors such as functionality, problem-solving approach, technical implementation, usability, creativity, and quality of the live demonstration.
  • The judges' decision regarding evaluation, penalties, qualification, and final results will be final and binding.
  • In case of a tie, the organizers may use additional evaluation criteria or a tie-breaker challenge/demonstration.
  • The organizers reserve the right to modify the event procedure when required for technical, safety, or operational reasons.

Event Format:

  • Team Size: 2–4 members
  • Duration: 8 hours
  • Event Type: On-site Software Hackathon

Challenge Flow:

  • Problem Reveal
    • The problem statement is announced at the beginning of the event. Teams start from scratch and develop a solution to the assigned real-world problem.
  • Development Phase
    • Teams design, code, test, and refine their software solution during the 8-hour hackathon.
  • Buffs & Debuffs
    • Four times during the event, a wheel determines a common challenge or advantage for the entire hall. Each Buff/Debuff remains active for 30 minutes.
    • Examples of possible restrictions include:
    • Voice-only coding
    • No Enter key
    • Whisper-mode communication

The same condition applies to all teams simultaneously.

  • Submission
    • Teams submit their completed working solution within the specified deadline.
  • Live Judging & Dem
    • Teams demonstrate their working product to the judges. Evaluation is conducted live rather than through recorded demos or presentation-only submissions.
  • Results
    • The highest-performing teams are selected based on the organizers' judging criteria.

Venue: Ramaiah Technology Campus, Bengaluru
Registration Fee: ₹200 per team
Prizes: ₹15,000 (1st) | ₹10,000 (2nd) | ₹7,000 (3rd)
